about: workflow:move-table-rows-into-the-stores-own-records: moves the rows a person's own store kept in tables into the store's own records, in whole batches, leaving a record that a newer write made and dropping a table only when it is empty. It replaces tools/move-the-rows-a-persons-store-kept-in-tables (src/tables-into-records.mjs), whose whole job was copying table rows into the retired record store (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do).

payload.label: Move table rows into the store's own records
payload.job: Move the rows a person's own store kept in tables of their own into the store's own records: the rows needed at once first, then the rest in whole batches; a record that a newer write already made is left as that write made it; the table is let go only when it is empty.
payload.produces: The store's own records for the moved rows, proven on the example attempts, with each batch's moved and left rows and each read back, and the source table gone at the end.

source.from: tools/move-the-rows-a-persons-store-kept-in-tables (src/tables-into-records.mjs, moved from the old repository), read on trillion-workshop origin/main 13c05f2c8c
source.note: Only the keeping is the store's job: the rows of one table become its records, batch by batch, with a progress place so a reset loses nothing. The move runs once per store, on the person's request; the old record log and its tables are not named. Its invariants are kept as the intent: nothing names a table or a kind of record (the caller says which rows move), a record that exists is never replaced, a partial first move is not presented as complete, and progress is written only with the batch it covers.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

tables.description: The person's own tables to move, each {table (its name in the store), first_column (the column that marks rows needed at once), record_of (the record id each row becomes)}

operations.description: Operations to run this time: start {limit} (rows needed at once, at most limit), step {limit} (one batch, at most limit rows), read {id}, source_left

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of its tables and records. Submit the names of the tables found and the names of any records the move already made (moved_before), or empty lists.

steps.title: Make the store's own records, once
steps.do: When the look step found no records of the move, make the store's own records for it in its own form: a progress place per table (where the rows needed at once have reached, and where the rest have reached), a record per moved row written with the record_of id, and a rule that a record which exists is never written over. Make the move's batches whole: a batch is written out only with the progress it covers, so a reset loses only what was brought in since the last write and the next step brings it again. Refuse a limit outside 1 to 128 and an empty table name. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the objects on the example attempts
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, make one example table notes with rows n1 (first, body first note), n2 (body second), n3 (body third) and n4 (body fourth), where the record note:n2 already exists with the body newer second, then run these operations in order: [{"op": "start", "limit": 2}, {"op": "step", "limit": 2}, {"op": "step", "limit": 2}, {"op": "step", "limit": 2}, {"op": "read", "id": "note:n2"}, {"op": "read", "id": "note:n4"}, {"op": "source_left"}, {"op": "step", "limit": 0}]. Answers: start gives {moved, first_ready} for the rows first_column marks, limited to limit; step gives {moved, left_newer, dropped} for one batch in id order: a row whose record exists is left (listed in left_newer) and its table row is taken away, any other row becomes its record and is taken away, and when the table is empty it is dropped and dropped is true; read gives the body of the record, source_left the number of rows left in the table; a limit outside 1 to 128 is refused. Then remove the throwaway place. Submit answers: one per attempt, in order, exactly as the answers above.

checks.says: Each attempt gives the answer the intent says

steps.title: Keep this run's moves
steps.do: Run each item of operations through the store's own objects, in order, and read back every record each move made or left. With no operations, submit empty lists. Submit answers (one per operation, as in the prove step) and found_records (each record id read back).

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes the records the move made and its progress places; the person's table rows are the person's own and are not kept by the move.
